subject: SS Edmund Fitzgerald
hook: SS EDMUND FITZGERALD IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: The SS Edmund Fitzgerald was not just a rugged freighter, but a luxury liner for guests, featuring air-conditioned crew quarters, leather swivel chairs, and candlelit dinners with mess-jacketed stewards.
angle_support: By ore freighter standards, the interior of Edmund Fitzgerald was luxurious. Her J. L. Hudson Company–designed furnishings included deep pile carpeting, tiled bathrooms, drapes over the portholes, and leather swivel chairs in the guest lounge.
Once each trip, the captain held a candlelight dinner for the guests, complete with mess-jacketed stewards and special "clamdigger" punch.
title: Edmund Fitzgerald: The Luxury Liner Hidden in a Freighter
description: Most people think of the Edmund Fitzgerald as a massive ore‑carrying freighter, but its cabins were outfitted like a boutique hotel. Deep carpets, leather chairs, air‑conditioned quarters, and candlelit dinners turned it into a floating luxury experience.
narration: SS EDMUND FITZGERALD IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture a rugged freighter, a plain steel box hauling ore across the Great Lakes. It was more like a floating hotel with plush seats and candlelight meals for guests. The ship’s interior featured deep‑pile carpeting, tiled baths, drapes, leather swivel chairs, two guest staterooms, air‑conditioned crew quarters, a large galley feeding two dining rooms, and nightly candlelight dinners served by mess‑jacketed stewards for the guests. A freighter that also served as a luxury liner on the lakes daily.
